statement: US newsroom employment fell 26% between 2008 and 2020, with newspaper newsrooms alone shrinking 57%, from roughly 71,000 jobs to about 31,000.
evidence_quote: Newsroom employment in the United States has dropped by 26% since 2008.

statement: US newspaper advertising revenue fell from about $49.4 billion in 2005 to roughly $9.8 billion in 2022, a decline of about 80%.
evidence_quote: The total estimated advertising revenue for the newspaper industry in 2022 was $9.8 billion, based on the Center's analysis of financial statements for publicly traded newspaper companies.

statement: US daily newspaper circulation, print and digital combined, was 20.9 million in 2022, down 8% (weekday) and 10% (Sunday) from 2021.
evidence_quote: In 2022, estimated total U.S. daily newspaper circulation (print and digital combined) was 20.9 million for both weekday and Sunday, down 8% and 10% respectively from 2021.

statement: Close to 3,500 US newspapers have closed since 2005, and 213 counties are now news deserts with no local news outlet, up from 206 the year before.
publisher: Medill Local News Initiative, Northwestern University
evidence_quote: Close to 3,500 newspapers have vanished, leaving one in every four Americans with limited access to a local print newspaper.

statement: Some 50 million Americans live in counties with either no local news source or only one, once the 213 news deserts and 1,524 one-source counties are combined.
publisher: Medill Local News Initiative, Northwestern University
evidence_quote: In another 1,524 counties, there's only one remaining news source. Taken together, some 50 million Americans have limited to no access to local news.

statement: Global trust in the news was 40% in 2025, unchanged for a third consecutive year.
publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, University of Oxford
evidence_quote: Overall trust in the news (40%) has remained stable for the third year in a row, even if it is still four points lower overall than it was at the height of the Coronavirus pandemic.

statement: Selective avoidance of the news remained near an all-time high in 2025, with 40% of people saying they sometimes or often avoid it.
publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, University of Oxford
evidence_quote: Selective news avoidance remains close to its all-time high (40%), with respondents saying that they sometimes or often avoid the news.

statement: In the United States in 2025, social media and video networks overtook both television news and news websites as a source of news for the first time.
publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, University of Oxford
evidence_quote: The proportion accessing news via social media and video networks in the United States (54%) is sharply up – overtaking both TV news (50%) and news websites/apps (48%) for the first time.

statement: A 2018 study of Twitter cascades found that false stories spread significantly farther, faster and deeper than true stories, taking true stories six times as long to reach 1,500 people.
evidence_quote: It took the truth about six times as long as falsehood to reach 1500 people and 20 times as long as falsehood to reach a cascade depth of 10.

statement: A 2022 industry analysis estimated that programmatic advertisers directed about $2.6 billion a year worldwide to websites that publish misinformation and disinformation.
evidence_quote: The misinformation industry is booming–with $2.6 billion in estimated advertising revenue being sent to publishers of misinformation and disinformation each year by programmatic advertisers.

statement: In September 2024, the US Department of Justice announced the seizure of 32 internet domains used in a Russian government-directed influence campaign that had impersonated US news sites.
evidence_quote: The Justice Department today announced the ongoing seizure of 32 internet domains used in Russian government-directed foreign malign influence campaigns colloquially referred to as 'Doppelganger.'

statement: The US intelligence community's 2025 assessment describes Russian information operations aimed at sowing doubt in US democratic processes, alongside comparable Chinese and Iranian activity.
publisher: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
evidence_quote: Moscow uses influence activities to counter threats, including by stoking political discord in the West, sowing doubt in democratic processes and U.S. global leadership.

statement: ProPublica's Local Reporting Network reimburses a partner newsroom for a reporter's full salary, up to $80,000 for 2026 and $82,500 for 2027, plus benefits, to fund a single yearlong investigation.
evidence_quote: We will reimburse a news organization for the salary of the selected reporter (up to $80,000 for 2026 and $82,500 for 2027, plus a benefits stipend).

statement: The Society of Professional Journalists' Code of Ethics defines ethical journalism as accurate, fair and thorough, requiring verification before publication.
evidence_quote: Ethical journalism strives to ensure the free exchange of information that is accurate, fair and thorough. Take responsibility for the accuracy of their work. Verify information before releasing it.

statement: Thomson Reuters' Trust Principles require that the integrity, independence and freedom from bias of its reporting be preserved at all times.
evidence_quote: The integrity, independence, and freedom from bias of Thomson Reuters shall at all times be fully preserved.
